Setup configures the\n\u003ca href=\"/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#supported-agents\"\u003esupported agents\u003c/a\u003e; other clients can use\n\u003ca href=\"/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#mcp-registry\"\u003emanual MCP registration\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/details\u003e\n\u003cdetails\u003e\n\u003csummary\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDo I need Hopper, Ghidra or IDA?\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/summary\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDeep native analysis uses one of them. On macOS, a first-run dialog may\nask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the\nsame user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open\nHopper manually if needed. JavaScript/Electron analysis\nrecovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to\nwrite and test an implementation; the \u003ca href=\"#showcases\"\u003eshowcases\u003c/a\u003e give worked examples.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/details\u003e\n\u003cdetails\u003e\n\u003csummary\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDoes REA upload my app?\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/summary\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eREA analyzes targets locally. class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="perf(mcp): keep Playwright and type-only imports off MCP startup (#1691)

* fix(build): emit no runtime imports for type-only bindings

Under verbatimModuleSyntax, an import whose specifiers all carry inline
`type` modifiers compiles to `import {} from "..."`, a side-effect import
that still resolves and evaluates the module. 78 compiled modules carried
one, including `import {} from "playwright-core"` in the browser scenario
session, which loaded Playwright's module graph at MCP startup.

Use top-level `import type` for these bindings and enable oxlint's
typescript/no-import-type-side-effects rule so the pattern cannot return.

Refs #1685

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(mcp): load Playwright when a scenario launches, not at startup

The browser scenario and Electron active providers are constructed before
the stdio server serves, and both bound Playwright's launchers at module
load. Resolve `chromium` and `_electron` from playwright-core when a
capture opens instead, as the web module resolver already does.

MCP startup now resolves 1,312 modules (4,902 resolutions) instead of
1,598 (6,076) before reading the first request, and no longer loads
playwright-core. Provider construction, the tool catalog, and capability
inventory are unchanged.

A boundary test spawns the stdio server, initializes, lists tools, and
asserts playwright-core and isomorphic-git were not resolved; the CLI
probe now exercises the real launch path to prove detection.

Closes #1685

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="feat(kuna): serve procedures, pseudocode and assembly from Kuna exports (#3854)

* feat(kuna): serve procedures, pseudocode and assembly from Kuna exports

Register Kuna as a bring-your-own deep-analysis provider. It answers
list_documents, list_procedures, search_procedures, procedure_address,
address_name, procedure_pseudo_code, procedure_assembly and
analyze_function (and batch_decompile through composition) from the
verified project export. While a cold export builds in the background,
pseudocode comes from a single-function `kuna decompile` run on a private
copy and says so; assembly and data names wait for the export.

Each answer records its source and file span in raw_result, limitations
are scoped per operation, and the session-owned export is stopped on
close unless another session still waits for it. The literal/regex
procedure search predicate moves from the IDA runner into a shared
domain helper. `npm run verify:kuna` adds a real-provider lane with an
optional Ghidra comparison.

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): refuse a Ghidra comparison without caller-built targets

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): retry owned cleanup and keep answers bound to the opened Kuna

- Re-verify the Kuna executable's digest before every launch (memoized by
  file identity), so no answer names one build while another produced it.
- Keep the process supervisor of an unproven stop, and retry it on every
  later close in both the session and the cache; a failed close keeps
  failing until the stop is proven instead of reporting success.
- Report an abandoned export's retained cleanup from session close.
- Forget and rebuild an adopted export whose files another REA process
  evicted, instead of failing every later read.
- Close a private copy whose setup failed, and retry failed removals.
- Let the session own the shared quick inventory; each caller only stops
  waiting when it cancels.
- Report a failed export as `failed` with its reason.
- Lane: release the MCP client when open_binary rejects a target, and accept
  either valid source for the first answer.

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): drain session requests before releasing workspaces

Combine caller cancellation with session shutdown and wait for active reads before releasing their process supervisors or private inputs. Retain unproven cleanup for later close attempts. Measure UTF-8 reply bytes without implying model token usage.

* feat(kuna): serve procedures, pseudocode and assembly from Kuna exports

Register Kuna as a bring-your-own deep-analysis provider. It answers
list_documents, list_procedures, search_procedures, procedure_address,
address_name, procedure_pseudo_code, procedure_assembly and
analyze_function (and batch_decompile through composition) from the
verified project export. While a cold export builds in the background,
pseudocode comes from a single-function `kuna decompile` run on a private
copy and says so; assembly and data names wait for the export.

Each answer records its source and file span in raw_result, limitations
are scoped per operation, and the session-owned export is stopped on
close unless another session still waits for it. The literal/regex
procedure search predicate moves from the IDA runner into a shared
domain helper. `npm run verify:kuna` adds a real-provider lane with an
optional Ghidra comparison.

complete detached-PGP package verification under the stable publisher primary
key, and authenticated package evidence for offline admission. Share parsed
publisher facts across approved setup, doctor and the pre-execution guard.
Preserve existing ownership, cancellation, private-display and cleanup rules.

and retain publisher cleanup through cancellation and shutdown. Exercise cold
offline verification without reusing process-local proof state. Serialize
approved cache publication across processes, restore old evidence on failure,
and share the existing lease owner from process without changing its identities.

24.04 official Hopper 6.6.0 setup/CLI/MCP, offline ordinary-user admission,
launcher mutation rejection, and cold/warm verification measurements. Official
RPM metadata mismatch is tracked separately in #3578 and fails closed.

BREAKING CHANGE: Older Linux Hopper builds admitted by the fixed allowlist
now require retained publisher-signed package evidence or an approved update
to the current public demo. Update explicit HOPPER_LAUNCHER_PATH values when
migrating; the live feed exposes only its current release.

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="perf(catalog): record default catalog digests at build time (#4041)

Every `doctor`, `mcp doctor` and MCP server that reports or compares its
catalog identity rebuilt all advertised JSON Schemas and canonicalized
them to compute the default digests, about 200 ms of CPU per process.
The default (full input and output schema) catalog is a deterministic
function of the compiled contracts and pinned schema converter, so
compilation now records it once into dist and the runtime reuses it.
Compact and output-schema-off identities, and source runs, still compute
their digests on first use.

Refs #3813

<p dir="auto">See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project.</p>
<p dir="auto">REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion.</p>
<p dir="auto">Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong><a href="https://rea.tools/" rel="nofollow">Visit the REA website</a></strong> for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies.</p>
</blockquote>

<p dir="auto">On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron
analysis require a procps-compatible <code>ps</code> on REA's <code>PATH</code> for process ownership
checks. Recovery steps are in <code>docs/installation.md</code> under
"Linux owned-process prerequisite".</p>

<p dir="auto">Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds
REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing
configuration. Restart your agent afterward.</p>
<p dir="auto">Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#supported-agents">other agents</a>. See
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md">installation and setup</a> for provider configuration and
manual MCP registration.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How REA works</h2><a id="user-content-how-rea-works" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How REA works" href="#how-rea-works"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code.
REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up
questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation.
CLI commands use the same workflows.</p>

<p dir="auto">Static JavaScript and .NET inspection read the supplied files without running
the application. Runtime capture runs or interacts with the selected target
using your user permissions; each runtime guide describes its effects.</p>
<p dir="auto">For offline native-binary inspection, REA also supports caller-supplied GNU
objdump and Rizin. See the <a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/reverse-engineering-tools.md">reverse-engineering tools guide</a>
for provider setup, CLI commands, and Evidence limitations. REA does not install
or update either provider.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a id="user-content-choosing-a-deep-analysis-provider"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Native formats and host support vary by provider. See
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#hopper">Hopper and Ghidra setup</a>, the
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/ida-provider.md">IDA guide</a> (including an optional native MCP bridge), the
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/kuna-provider.md">Kuna decompiler guide</a>, and
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/windows-ghidra-p0.md">experimental Windows Ghidra support</a>.
Ghidra also supports <a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/ghidra-dos.md">16-bit DOS analysis</a>.
For large binaries, raise the provider's startup deadline with
<code>REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS</code> or <code>REA_HOPPER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS</code>.
For provider selection, see the <a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/cli.md#choose-a-provider">CLI guide</a>.
Check <a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#released-package-and-main">release availability</a>
for features added since the latest npm release.</p>

<details>
<summary><strong>Which agents can use REA?</strong></summary>
<p dir="auto">Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#supported-agents">supported agents</a>; other clients can use
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#mcp-registry">manual MCP registration</a>.</p>
</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>Do I need Hopper, Ghidra or IDA?</strong></summary>
<p dir="auto">Deep native analysis uses one of them. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection
work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval;
Ghidra and IDA use your existing installations. See <a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#hopper">provider setup</a>.</p>
</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>Do I need to start Hopper first?</strong></summary>
<p dir="auto">REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may
ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the
same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open
Hopper manually if needed. See
<a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting">Hopper startup and troubleshooting</a>.</p>
</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>What does installing the skill from skills.sh do?</strong></summary>
<p dir="auto">The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use <code>npx rea-agents setup</code>
to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart
your agent. See <a href="/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/installation.md#skill-only-installation">skill-only installation</a>.</p>
</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>What code does REA return?</strong></summary>
<p dir="auto">Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis
recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to
write and test an implementation; the <a href="#showcases">showcases</a> give worked examples.</p>
</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>Does REA upload my app?</strong></summary>
<p dir="auto">REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its
model provider has its own data policy.</p>
</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>What should I do if I hit a bug?</strong></summary>
<p dir="auto">Update first; a recent release may already fix it.</p>
<p dir="auto">For a CLI installed with <code>npm install --global</code> or <code>bun add --global</code>:</p>
